$comment: Accepted merge-gate policy for `main`. This file is the written intent;
`scripts/check-workflow-policy.mjs` is what makes it true. Offline it
reconciles this policy against the workflow files that actually produce the
contexts; with `--live` it also reads back the repository settings and the
`main` ruleset. Both directions fail: a context here that no workflow emits,
and a pull-request job that no entry claims.
`class` records the authority of a check, which is not the same question as
required     a merge gate; must be emitted on every ordinary pull request
staged       intended to become required, held back until observed stable
advisory     reports, never blocks (path-filtered or scheduled coverage)
automation   repository automation, not a statement about the change

components.name: rust
components.proves: The extension crate formats, passes clippy with warnings denied, passes `cargo test --locked`, and builds for `wasm32-wasip2` — the target the extension registry ships. It does not prove anything about Spring Tools behaviour.

components.name: coordinator
components.proves: Coordinator and repository-check tests pass, and the derivable records — contributors list, third-party notices, Spring Tools pin inventory — match the tree they describe.

components.name: review
components.proves: The dependency diff this pull request introduces carries no known advisory at moderate or above. Scoped to the diff only; the standing graph is Dependabot's.

components.name: workflow-security
components.proves: actionlint, zizmor and this policy check all pass, so no workflow carries a mutable action ref, a missing timeout, an unsafe `pull_request_target` checkout, or a context that has drifted from this file.

components.name: Platform Validation
components.proves: The canonical CI DAG invokes the reusable Platform Validation workflow on every pull request. Its internal fail-closed scope classifier preserves the reviewed path applicability: non-applicable or draft PRs return a successful no-op result, while applicable PRs require all six native platform legs and the independent JDK 21 runtime floor to succeed for the exact pull-request revision.

components.name: codeql-runtime
components.proves: Always-present read-only compatibility probe for the production-pinned CodeQL Actions runtime. Trusted-base fail-closed classification selects real execution only for CodeQL compatibility-sensitive changes; selected runs analyze the exact pull-request head with build-mode none, upload never and runner-local SARIF, then reuse the strict Actions SARIF verdict and prove the result cannot satisfy trusted release evidence.

contexts.proves: All six authoritative merge components for the exact pull-request revision completed successfully. Platform Validation and the CodeQL runtime compatibility probe are stable always-present components: their expensive work is conditional, but applicable failures, failed classification, cancelled/skipped/missing component results, or any other non-success keep Merge Gate closed.

Each Linux, macOS, and Windows x86_64/arm64 leg runs on its native GitHub-hosted architecture with JDK 25, Node 24, and Rust 1.98.0. Linux/macOS drive every existing coordinator contract directly; Windows drives every platform-neutral contract and proof-equivalent native path/wall-clock replacements for seven legacy fixture-bound forms. Every leg also runs the Java bridge self-test, native Rust tests and native path/wrapper checks; checksum-verifies then launches the canonical pinned Spring Tools runtime for real headless LSP initialize/open/completion/hover/shutdown traffic; and independently launches pinned JDT LS 1.60.0 with the canonical Spring 5.3 JDT bundle set plus the bridge built from the current source, asserting Spring/bridge delegate commands and executing the bridge remove command. This is headless integration evidence, not Zed desktop + official Java extension/proxy end-to-end evidence.

Under the declared JDK 21 floor on Linux x86_64, the canonical pinned Spring Tools runtime checksum-verifies, starts with the production Spring JVM launch vector, serves real headless LSP traffic and terminates; independently, pinned JDT LS 1.60.0 loads the canonical Spring 5.3 JDT bundles plus the current bridge, advertises their delegate commands and executes the bridge remove command. Host portability remains owned by the six-tuple `platform` matrix; this does not prove the Zed desktop + official Java extension/proxy path.

Internal aggregate of the reusable Platform Validation workflow. For applicable/manual runs it requires all six native platform legs and the independent JDK 21 floor; for non-applicable or draft pull requests it records a successful no-op. The repository ruleset still requires only the outer `Merge Gate`.

Scheduled weekly or deliberate manual four-language scan of exact protected-main SHA, original per-language SARIF, CodeQL query pack/analysis validation and a fail-closed High/Critical verdict. Java build-mode none does not cover Kotlin: detection fails if Kotlin sources appear. Deliberately not a PR context or merge blocker; Registry release operates under documented pre-publication operator hold.

Nothing about the change. Applies additive routing labels on `pull_request` for same-repository branches only; fork pull requests are intentionally skipped because their read-only token cannot write labels. It is automation metadata, never a merge gate.
